# Design: Make the role evaluation suite discriminate

## Context

`codev-evals` (`evals/`, archived change `2026-10-13-role-evaluation-suite`)
is a workspace crate that is never shipped. Following decision 0001, its
`case`, `score` and `report` modules are pure functions; `runner` and
`main` do the I/O. Today:

- `case::load` parses `case.yaml` (`serde_norway`, decision 0006, with
  `deny_unknown_fields`), checks the fixture files (UTF-8, 64 KiB) and that
  each expected location exists, on the fixture as a merged map of `base/`
  and `change/` (`Fixture::merged`).
- `score::review` matches with `Location::matched_by` alone, then
  `classify_unmatched` reuses that same location test for duplicates and
  cross-role findings.
- `observed.json` stores the whole `codev review --json` document under
  `review`; `ReviewFinding` reads only `id`, `title`, `role`, `step`,
  `severity`, `confidence`, `location`, `status`. The raw JSON already
  carries `recommendation` and `evidence` for every finding, the
  committed baseline included.
- The runner copies only `base/` and `change/` into the run directory:
  the role under evaluation never sees `case.yaml`.

Observed in the baseline (2026-10-13, 26 cases): recall 1.00 for every
role; 28 false positives, of which at least five trace back to a fixture
contradicting itself (see "Decision: The current fixtures are audited
against their baseline findings"); one location-only true positive
(`accessibility-code-icon-button`, R-accessibility-1).

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**

- A true positive means the role named the seeded defect, not merely
  something near it.
- A false positive means the role invented something, not that the
  fixture lied to it.
- Per role, a number that separates the obvious from the subtle, on
  defects and on decoys.
- Every judgement stays deterministic and runs without a model, so that
  `codev-evals score` re-scores any recorded run, the existing baseline
  included.

**Non-Goals:**

- Changing the review record format, the skills or any role in
  `assets/roles/`.
- A model-based judge of matches.
- Repeated runs or variance (still left for later).
- New thresholds per difficulty: the gates stay on totals until the new
  baseline shows what is reachable.

## Decisions

### Decision: The defect type is matched by declared terms, on title and recommendation

Each expected finding declares `terms` (one or more). A finding names the
defect when its title or recommendation, whitespace-collapsed and
lower-cased, contains one of the terms, normalized the same way. The
evidence is not searched: it quotes fixture code, which contains the
very tokens the terms would use (`alt`, `LIKE`, `retry`).

The match becomes one predicate, `Expected::matched_by(&ReviewFinding,
&Location) -> bool` in `case.rs` (location test, then term test), used
both by the matching loop and by `classify_unmatched`, so that "duplicate"
and "cross-role" follow the same definition as "true positive".
`ReviewFinding` gains `recommendation` (`#[serde(default)]`); the
observation format marker stays 1, since the field is already in every
recorded file.

Terms are written from the defect's vocabulary, several per defect to
cover usual paraphrases (for `image-without-alt`: `alt`, `text
alternative`, `alternative text`). The `category` key stays as a label
for the report; it does not take part in the match.

**Alternatives considered**:

- A `category` field in each finding of the review record — rejected: the
  record refuses unknown fields (`review_unknown_field`), and decision
  0002 makes `codev review --json` a public contract; changing it for the
  harness alone is out of proportion, and the role would have to guess a
  taxonomy it never sees.
- Matching on `category` against words of the title — a category such as
  `keyboard-and-name` is a label, not the words a reviewer uses.
- A model as judge — non-deterministic, costs a call per finding, and
  breaks "score again without a model".
- Regular expressions instead of substrings — more power than needed, and
  harder to review in a case file; substrings ignoring case and spacing
  cover the paraphrases seen in the baseline.

### Decision: Coherence is checked on cited paths, at load, in the pure core

`case::load` gains a check over the merged fixture: it extracts the code
spans of the change's `proposal.md`, `design.md`, `tasks.md` and
`specs/**/spec.md`, keeps the ones that look like a path (spec: a `/`, or
one of a fixed list of extensions; no space; not a URL), strips a
trailing `:line`, `:start-end` or `#heading`, and requires each to be a
file of the merged fixture, a directory prefix of one (a cited path
ending in `/`, or any prefix followed by `/`), or listed in the new
optional `planned` key. A `planned` path must be cited and must not
already exist in `base/` (a path that the change itself adds under
`change/` is legitimate, which is why only `base/` is tested). The check
is a pure function of the fixture map and the case, like the location
check next to it, and its error names the artifact and the path.

Only paths are checked mechanically. They are the commonest source of
false positives in the baseline (`web/src/settings/`, the CLI files of
`skeptic-control-small-flag`), and the only incoherence a program can
decide without understanding the plan.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Checking cited test names, functions or identifiers — needs a parser
  per stack and guesses what is an identifier; left to the audit below.
- A model-based "fixture lint" — non-deterministic and paid at every
  `cargo test`.
- No `planned` key, tolerating any path named after "create" in
  `tasks.md` — a heuristic on prose; an explicit list is reviewable.

### Decision: Difficulty is a required key, and coverage asks for one subtle case of each kind

`case.yaml` gains `difficulty: obvious | subtle`, required, so that every
existing case states it (all 26 are `obvious`: the baseline found every
one of their defects, and their controls hold nothing that looks like a
defect). `coverage_gaps` adds, for each reviewing role, a missing subtle
seeded case and a missing subtle control. `CaseScore` carries the
difficulty; `RoleScore` gains `by_difficulty: BTreeMap<Difficulty,
DifficultyScore>` (cases, expected, true positives, recall, false
positives), rendered as one extra table "Per role and difficulty" in
`report.md` and a `byDifficulty` object in `report.json`. Thresholds keep
reading the totals.

**Alternatives considered**:

- A third `kind`, `decoy` — conflates what the case is (seeded or clean)
  with how hard it is; a subtle seeded case would need a fourth kind.
- Weighting subtle defects in recall — hides the split the report is
  meant to show.

### Decision: Eighteen new cases, one subtle seeded and one decoy per role

Each new case is small, like the existing ones, and its summary says what
makes it subtle. Stacks are spread so that Rust, TypeScript and Python
each appear among the new cases.

| Role | Subtle seeded case | Decoy control |
|---|---|---|
| security | `security-code-path-traversal-after-normalize` — the path is checked before it is decoded, in another file | `security-control-allowlisted-order-by` — SQL built by concatenation from a closed allow-list of columns |
| privacy | `privacy-plan-hashed-email-to-vendor` — "anonymized" data is an unsalted hash of the e-mail, still personal data | `privacy-control-pseudonymous-metrics` — a user id in metrics, with a design that states purpose and retention |
| accessibility | `accessibility-code-focus-lost-on-close` — closing a dialog drops focus to `body` | `accessibility-control-decorative-image` — `alt=""` on a purely decorative image |
| performance | `performance-code-quadratic-dedup` — `Vec::contains` inside a loop over an import | `performance-control-small-fixed-loop` — a query in a loop over the seven days of a week |
| ops | `ops-plan-retry-without-idempotency` — retries are bounded, but on a non-idempotent call | `ops-control-intentional-infinite-loop` — a worker loop with shutdown signal and back-off |
| migration | `migration-code-default-changes-meaning` — a new column's default changes the meaning of existing rows | `migration-control-dropped-unused-column` — a column dropped after a release that stopped writing and reading it, documented |
| newcomer | `newcomer-code-misleading-name` — `is_valid` that also mutates its argument | `newcomer-control-dense-but-documented` — a compact algorithm with a comment citing its source |
| skeptic | `skeptic-plan-success-metric-unmeasurable` — the plan's success criterion cannot be observed with what it builds | `skeptic-control-justified-new-dependency` — a new dependency with alternatives weighed |
| tracer | `tracer-plan-requirement-without-scenario` — a requirement whose only scenario tests another one | `tracer-control-tasks-grouped-differently` — a complete plan whose tasks are grouped by file, not by requirement |

The identifiers are the intended ones; the implementer may adjust a
fixture's details, provided the table's intent is kept and the summary
says it.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Making the existing cases harder in place — loses the comparison with
  the 2026-10-13 baseline, and leaves no measure of obvious defects.
- Two subtle cases per role — doubles the cost of a run (about 0.37 USD a
  case) before knowing whether one already discriminates.

### Decision: The current fixtures are audited against their baseline findings

Every high-confidence false positive of the 2026-10-13 baseline is read
against its fixture. When the finding is true of the fixture — the
fixture contradicts itself or promises what it does not hold — the
fixture is corrected so that the defect disappears; when the finding is a
real invention, the fixture stays. At least these are corrected:

- `skeptic-control-small-flag`: the plan names CLI files the fixture does
  not hold, and a task cites a test nothing creates.
- `skeptic-plan-scope-creep`: `proposal.md#Impact` names
  `web/src/settings/`, absent.
- `newcomer-code-clever-one-liner`: the task cites a verification test
  that does not exist.
- `skeptic-plan-unsupported-assumption`: `## Domains` ticks nothing
  although the plan deletes customers' personal data.
- `performance-control-batched-query`: the 100-item cart bound the code
  relies on is not in the fixture.

The coherence check prevents the path cases from coming back; the others
are recorded in each case's summary when they shaped the fix.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Re-labelling such findings as expected — would reward roles for
  pointing at accidents of authoring, not at the seeded defects.

### Decision: The scoring is proven on the old observations before the baseline is recorded again

Because matching runs on recorded data, the new scoring is first applied
to the 2026-10-13 observations (with `terms` and `difficulty` added to the
existing cases): `R-accessibility-1` of `accessibility-code-icon-button`
must no longer match `image-without-alt`, and `R-accessibility-3` must
match it instead. That before/after is kept in the pull request. Only
then are the fixtures corrected, the new cases added and the whole suite
run again into `evals/baseline/`, whose test (`the_baseline_agrees_with_
the_scoring`) keeps the committed report honest.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Terms too narrow: a role names the defect in other words and is scored
  a miss] → several terms per defect, chosen from the titles of the old
  baseline where it found the defect; any miss in the new baseline is
  read by hand before the baseline is committed, and terms widened when
  the role did name the defect.
- [Terms too broad: a common word such as `query` lets any finding
  match] → terms name the defect, not the subject; the authoring guide in
  `roles.md` says so, and the re-scoring of the old baseline must not
  create new true positives on findings about another defect.
- [A decoy holds a real defect, so a sharp role is punished] → each
  decoy's summary states why it is clean; a high-confidence finding on a
  decoy in the new baseline is read by hand, and if it is right, the
  fixture is fixed rather than the finding counted.
- [The coherence check refuses a legitimate citation, e.g. an external
  path] → the extension list is closed and short, `planned` covers files
  to create, and an external URL is never a path; a refusal names the path
  so the author can rephrase it outside a code span.
- [The suite grows from 26 to 44 cases, about 16 USD a full run] →
  `--out` resumption and the per-case budget already bound it; the suite
  stays on demand only.

## Migration Plan

1. Scoring and loading changes, with `terms` and `difficulty` added to the
   26 existing cases; re-score the old observations and compare.
2. Correct the incoherent fixtures; the coherence check passes on the
   suite.
3. Add the eighteen cases.
4. Record the baseline again (`codev-evals run --out evals/baseline
   --rerun`) and commit it with its report.
5. Update the Roles chapter in `docs/en` and `docs/fr`.

Rollback: revert the change; the old baseline is in history and still
scores under the old code.

## Open Questions

None: the assumptions the request left open are stated in the proposal.

# Proposal: Make the role evaluation suite discriminate

## Why

The baseline recorded on 2026-10-13 (`evals/baseline/report.md`) gives every
role a recall of 1.00: the seeded defects are all obvious, so the suite
cannot tell a sharp role from a dull one. Its failures come from false
positives, several of which are caused by the fixtures themselves — the
`skeptic-control-small-flag` plan names CLI files the fixture does not hold,
`skeptic-plan-scope-creep` names a `web/src/settings/` that does not exist,
`newcomer-code-clever-one-liner` cites a test that is absent. And a finding
matches an expected one on its location alone: in
`accessibility-code-icon-button`, "Delete action is a clickable div" was
scored as the true positive of `image-without-alt`, one line away. The
scores are therefore not yet a reliable reference for changing a role,
which is the suite's whole purpose.

## What Changes

- **Fixture coherence is checked at load.** A path a case's planning
  artifacts cite in code spans must exist in the fixture, or be declared by
  the case as a path the plan intends to create; otherwise the case is
  refused, naming the file, the path and the citing artifact. The
  incoherent fixtures of the current suite are corrected.
- **A finding also matches on the type of defect.** Each expected finding
  declares `terms`, words or phrases that name its defect; a finding
  matches only when it is of the right role, at a matching location, and
  its title or recommendation contains one of the terms. A finding at the
  right place that names another defect is no longer counted as finding
  the expected one.
- **Cases declare their difficulty.** `case.yaml` gains a `difficulty`,
  `obvious` or `subtle`. A subtle seeded case hides a defect that needs
  reasoning across files or about a non-obvious consequence; a subtle
  control — a decoy — is clean code or a sound plan that holds what looks
  like a defect but is not (a string-built SQL query over a fixed
  allow-list, a retry loop that is bounded elsewhere…).
- **Coverage requires subtle cases.** Every reviewing role needs at least
  one subtle seeded case and one decoy control, in addition to the present
  minimum. About eighteen cases are added.
- **The report splits by difficulty.** Per role, recall and false positives
  are also given for obvious and subtle cases, so that a role that only
  finds the obvious is visible.
- The baseline is recorded again against the new suite and scoring.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

### Modified Capabilities

- `role-evaluation`

### Removed Capabilities

## Impact

- `evals/src/case.rs` — new keys (`terms`, `difficulty`, `planned`), the
  coherence check, the coverage rule.
- `evals/src/score.rs` — matching by type, per-difficulty measures.
- `evals/src/report.rs` — the per-difficulty columns in `report.md` and
  `report.json`.
- `evals/cases/` — every existing seeded case gains `terms` and every case
  gains `difficulty`; the incoherent fixtures are corrected; about eighteen
  new cases.
- `evals/baseline/` — recorded again (one run of the whole suite, roughly
  15 USD at the current cost per case).
- `docs/en/src/roles.md` and `docs/fr/src/roles.md` — how a case declares
  its terms and difficulty, where the Roles chapter describes the
  measurement.
- No change to codev's binaries, to the review record format or to the
  skills: observations already hold each finding's title and
  recommendation, so recorded runs stay scorable without a model.

Assumptions, made without a user to ask:

- The defect type is matched by declared terms rather than by a `category`
  field in the review record: the review record refuses unknown fields
  (`review_unknown_field`), and adding one would change codev's public
  format for the sake of the test harness.
- Coherence is checked mechanically on cited paths only; the other
  inconsistencies seen in the baseline (a `## Domains` that contradicts the
  plan, a scenario broader than its requirement) are corrected by hand in
  the fixtures, not detected.
- The thresholds (`--min-recall` 0.5, `--max-false-positives` 2,
  `--min-evidence` 0.8) stay as they are; they are revisited once the new
  baseline shows where the roles stand.
- The `tracer` gets a subtle seeded case and a decoy control too: uniform
  coverage is simpler to state and to check.
- Domains: there is no diff to go by yet (the change holds only planning
  files), so they are ticked by judgement; the change touches the internal
  evaluation harness only.

## Domains

None

## Release note

None

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: A case declares its fixture, its step, its role and what it expects

The repository SHALL hold an evaluation suite under `evals/cases/`, one
directory per case, named by the case's id. A case holds:

- `case.yaml` — `role` (the role evaluated), `step` (`plan.challenge`,
  `code.review` or `plan.trace`), `change` (the change's name), `stacks`
  (the fixture's languages), `kind` (`seeded` or `control`),
  `difficulty` (`obvious` or `subtle`), a one-line `summary`, optionally
  `planned` (the paths the change's plan intends to create), and either
  `expected` (for `plan.challenge` and `code.review`) or `checks` (for
  `plan.trace`);
- `base/` — the fixture project as it is on its default branch;
- `change/` — the files the change adds or modifies, its planning
  artifacts under `_codev/changes/<change>/` included.

An expected finding states its `id`, `severity`, `category`, one or more
`locations`, in the review record's location syntax: `path:line` or
`path:start-end` relative to the project for code, `<file>#<heading>` or
`<file>` relative to the change's directory for the plan, and one or more
`terms`: words or phrases that name its defect, any one of which a
finding reporting that defect would use. A `plan.trace` case states
`checks`: `fixed` entries (a file of the fixture and a text it must
contain after the run) and `unchanged` paths (files the run must leave as
they were).

A `subtle` seeded case holds a defect that cannot be seen on the cited
lines alone; a `subtle` control holds a construct that resembles a defect
of its role and is not one. The summary of a subtle case SHALL say what
makes it subtle.

A case SHALL be refused, naming the case and the reason, when: a key is
unknown; `difficulty` is missing or not `obvious` or `subtle`; the role
does not serve the step; a `seeded` case expects nothing or a `control`
expects something; an expected finding has no term, or an empty one; an
expected location names a file absent from the fixture, a line beyond its
end or a heading it does not have; a fixture file is not UTF-8 text or is
larger than 64 KiB; the fixture is incoherent, as the requirement on
fixture coherence defines it.

#### Scenario: The repository's suite is well formed

- **GIVEN** the cases under `evals/cases/`
- **WHEN** the test suite of `codev-evals` runs
- **THEN** every case loads, every expected location exists in its
  fixture, and every fixture is coherent

#### Scenario: An unknown key

- **GIVEN** a `case.yaml` with the key `expect` instead of `expected`
- **WHEN** the case is loaded
- **THEN** it is refused, and the message names `expect`

#### Scenario: A location beyond the end of the file

- **GIVEN** a seeded case expecting `src/users.ts:120` and a fixture
  whose `src/users.ts` has 40 lines
- **WHEN** the case is loaded
- **THEN** it is refused, and the message names the file and the line

#### Scenario: A binary fixture file

- **GIVEN** a case whose `change/` holds a file that is not UTF-8 text
- **WHEN** the case is loaded
- **THEN** it is refused, and the message names the file

#### Scenario: An expected finding without terms

- **GIVEN** a seeded case whose expected finding `sql-injection` has
  locations and no `terms`
- **WHEN** the case is loaded
- **THEN** it is refused, and the message names `sql-injection` and
  `terms`

#### Scenario: A case without difficulty

- **GIVEN** a `case.yaml` without the key `difficulty`
- **WHEN** the case is loaded
- **THEN** it is refused, and the message names `difficulty`

### Requirement: The suite covers every reviewing role

The suite SHALL hold, for each expert (`security`, `privacy`,
`accessibility`, `performance`, `ops`, `migration`), at least two seeded
cases and one control; for the `newcomer` and the `skeptic`, at least two
seeded cases and one control; for the `tracer`, at least one seeded case
and one control. In addition, every one of these roles SHALL have at
least one `subtle` seeded case and one `subtle` control. Among the cases,
the stacks SHALL include Rust, TypeScript and Python.

#### Scenario: The repository's suite meets the minimum

- **GIVEN** the cases under `evals/cases/`
- **WHEN** the test suite of `codev-evals` runs
- **THEN** it passes

#### Scenario: A role without a control

- **GIVEN** a suite where the `ops` role has two seeded cases and no
  control
- **WHEN** its coverage is checked
- **THEN** the check fails and names `ops` and the missing control

#### Scenario: A role with only obvious cases

- **GIVEN** a suite where the `privacy` role has a subtle seeded case and
  only obvious controls
- **WHEN** its coverage is checked
- **THEN** the check fails and names `privacy` and the missing subtle
  control

### Requirement: What a role invents is counted, and only that

A finding that matches no expected finding SHALL be:

- a **false positive** of its role when its confidence is `high`;
- **unreported** when its confidence is `low` — the human never sees it —
  counted apart, not as a false positive;
- a **duplicate**, not a false positive, when it matches an expected
  finding of its role already matched;
- **cross-role**, not a false positive, when it matches an expected
  finding of another role.

"Matches" here has the meaning of the matching requirement — role aside
for cross-role —, defect type included: a finding at an expected location
whose title and recommendation name none of its terms is neither a
duplicate nor cross-role.

In a `control` case, every finding with a high confidence is a false
positive.

#### Scenario: A clean control

- **GIVEN** a `control` case whose record holds one `privacy` finding of
  high confidence and one of low confidence
- **WHEN** the case is scored
- **THEN** `privacy` has one false positive and one unreported finding

#### Scenario: The same defect raised twice

- **GIVEN** an expected finding and two findings of its role that both
  match it
- **WHEN** the case is scored
- **THEN** there is one true positive, one duplicate, and no false
  positive

#### Scenario: Another defect at the same place

- **GIVEN** an expected `accessibility` finding `image-without-alt` at
  `src/components/Toolbar.tsx:12` with the terms `alt` and `text
  alternative`, already matched, and a second high-confidence finding of
  that role at `src/components/Toolbar.tsx:13` titled "Delete target is
  too small"
- **WHEN** the case is scored
- **THEN** the second finding is a false positive, not a duplicate

### Requirement: The report is per role, in markdown and JSON, and the exit code follows thresholds

`codev-evals run` and `codev-evals score` SHALL write `report.md` and
`report.json` in their output directory, with, per role: the cases, the
expected findings, true positives, misses, false positives, unreported,
duplicates, cross-role findings, recall (true positives over expected),
evidence validity and severity agreement; then, per role and per
difficulty (`obvious`, `subtle`): the cases, the expected findings, the
true positives, the recall and the false positives; and per case: its
outcome, its difficulty, each finding's classification, the findings
whose status is no longer `open` and the files modified outside the
step. The model, date and versions of the run are those recorded when
the run started. The order is fixed — roles and cases by id, `obvious`
before `subtle` — so that the same observations give the same bytes.

A role SHALL fail when its recall is under `--min-recall` (default 0.5),
its false positives exceed `--max-false-positives` (default 2), or its
evidence validity is under `--min-evidence` (default 0.8); each threshold
can also be set by `CODEV_EVAL_MIN_RECALL`,
`CODEV_EVAL_MAX_FALSE_POSITIVES` and `CODEV_EVAL_MIN_EVIDENCE`, the flag
winning. The thresholds apply to the role's totals, all difficulties
together. The command SHALL exit with 0 when every role passes and no
case is in error, 1 otherwise, naming each failing role and measure, and
2 on an invalid threshold, an invalid case or a missing tool.

#### Scenario: Every role passes

- **GIVEN** observations where each role's recall, false positives and
  evidence validity meet the thresholds
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev-evals score <dir>`
- **THEN** it exits with 0 and writes both reports

#### Scenario: A role under the recall threshold

- **GIVEN** observations where `ops` finds one of four expected findings
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev-evals score <dir> --min-recall 0.5`
- **THEN** it exits with 1, and the message names `ops`, its recall
  0.25 and the threshold

#### Scenario: An invalid threshold

- **GIVEN** `CODEV_EVAL_MIN_RECALL=lots`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev-evals score <dir>`
- **THEN** it exits with 2 and names the variable

#### Scenario: A role that only finds the obvious

- **GIVEN** observations where `security` finds both expected findings of
  its obvious seeded cases and neither of its subtle seeded case
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev-evals score <dir>`
- **THEN** the report gives `security` a recall of 1.00 on obvious cases
  and 0.00 on subtle ones, besides its overall recall

## REMOVED Requirements

### Requirement: A finding matches an expected finding by role and location

**Reason**: Matching on the location alone credits a role with a defect
it did not name, as soon as it reports anything nearby. Replaced by the
requirement "A finding matches an expected finding by role, location and
defect type", which keeps every rule of this one and adds the type.
**Migration**: Every expected finding of a case declares `terms`; the
baseline is recorded again.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: A finding matches an expected finding by role, location and defect type

A finding of the review record SHALL match an expected finding when it
was written by the expected finding's role (its `### <role-id>` section),
its location matches one of the expected locations, and its title or its
recommendation contains one of the expected finding's terms.

Locations match as follows:

- code: the same path — `\` read as `/`, a leading `./` ignored — and
  line ranges that overlap once the expected range is widened by two
  lines on each side;
- plan: the same file and, when the expected location names a heading,
  the same heading, compared ignoring case and runs of whitespace; an
  expected location without a heading matches any location in that file.

A term is contained when it appears in the title or the recommendation
ignoring case and runs of whitespace; the evidence is not searched, since
it quotes the fixture rather than naming the defect.

Each expected finding is matched at most once, by the first matching
finding in record order, expected findings taken in case order. A
matched expected finding is a **true positive**; one left unmatched is a
**miss**. The severity of a true positive is compared with the expected
one and counted as **severity agreement**; it does not decide the match.

#### Scenario: Overlapping lines

- **GIVEN** an expected `security` finding at `src/users.ts:12-14` with

### Requirement: A fixture is coherent with the plan it carries

A case's fixture SHALL be coherent: every path cited in a code span
(between backticks) of the change's planning artifacts — `proposal.md`,
`design.md`, `tasks.md` and the delta specs — SHALL either name a file or
a directory of the fixture, `base/` and `change/` merged, or be listed in
the case's `planned`. A code span counts as a path when it holds no space,
is not a URL, and either contains a `/` or ends with one of the
extensions `.rs`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.py`, `.sql`, `.html`, `.css`,
`.md`, `.toml`, `.yaml`, `.yml` or `.json`; a trailing `:line` or
`:start-end` is ignored, and so is a trailing `#<heading>`. Every path listed in
`planned` SHALL be cited by one of the planning artifacts and SHALL NOT
already exist in `base/`.

An incoherent case is refused, naming the case, the planning artifact,
the path, and whether it is missing from the fixture or listed in
`planned` without being cited or while already existing.

#### Scenario: The plan names a directory the fixture does not have

- **GIVEN** a case whose `proposal.md` names `web/src/settings/` in its
  Impact, a fixture without that directory, and no `planned`
- **WHEN** the case is loaded
- **THEN** it is refused, and the message names `proposal.md` and
  `web/src/settings/`

#### Scenario: A file the plan will create

- **GIVEN** a `plan.challenge` case whose `tasks.md` names
  `src/cli/quiet.rs`, absent from the fixture, and listed in `planned`
- **WHEN** the case is loaded
- **THEN** it loads

#### Scenario: A cited line of an existing file

- **GIVEN** a case whose `design.md` names `src/import.rs:14-41` and a
  fixture holding `src/import.rs`
- **WHEN** the case is loaded
- **THEN** the path is coherent

#### Scenario: A planned path that already exists

- **GIVEN** a case listing `src/api.rs` in `planned` and a `base/` that
  holds `src/api.rs`
- **WHEN** the case is loaded
- **THEN** it is refused, and the message names `src/api.rs` and
  `planned`

#### Scenario: A span that is not a path

- **GIVEN** a case whose `design.md` names `--quiet`, `Option<String>` and
  `https://example.com/docs`
- **WHEN** the case is loaded
- **THEN** none of them is checked as a path
